messages.content: Write the first page of an onboarding document for a new backend engineer joining a payments team. Around 200 words.

output:
# Welcome to the Payments Team

You're joining us at a critical moment. Our payment processing systems handle millions of dollars daily across dozens of payment methods and corridors. Your work directly affects customer trust, business revenue, and reconciliation accuracy.

## What We Do

We maintain the backend systems that process customer payments, manage payment state across our platform, and reconcile transactions with payment providers. We own the API surface that other teams integrate with, the event streams that keep the organization synchronized, and the dashboards that catch problems before they become incidents.

## Day One

Your onboarding buddy will help you set up local development environment and the payment sandbox. You'll need access to: the private GitHub repos, staging payment accounts with our providers, and read access to production logs.

Spend your first week reading recent incidents and PRs. They show what matters: race conditions on idempotent retries, timing issues with provider webhooks, data consistency across services.

## Critical Paths

Start with the payment flow diagram in `/docs/architecture/payment-flow.md`. Then trace an actual payment through our code—follow the API handler, the event publishing, the reconciliation job. Talk to oncall about what breaks most often.

Our biggest operational risk right now is webhook ordering and duplicate detection. You'll touch that code soon.

**Questions? Ask in #payments-engineering. We review your first PRs carefully.**
